Red meat ant
Iridomyrmex sanguineus (Family Formicidae)
Targeted pests: A range of slow moving insects such as
caterpillars and beetles.
Description: Red-brown thorax with a green-black abdomen.
Size: 5–10 mm in length.
Biology and predatory activity: The complete life cycle takes about
28 days. These ants are predatory but they also feed on nectar as
well as tending scales, mealybugs and fluted scales for honeydew.
In situations when natural food sources are not available and in drier
areas, red meat ants can chew the margins of young leaves and are
sometimes regarded as pests.
These ants are usually seen near nests on bare ground or foraging on
plants for honeydew-secreting insects or various prey species.
caveat: This source is an Australian (Northern Territory) government field guide, not a Cambodia-specific MAFF publication. It is included as a supplementary international reference for visual identification and general pest/disease biology only. Species presence, seasonal timing (the guide's monthly monitoring calendars reflect the NT dry/wet season cycle), and any pesticide or chemical guidance are specific to northern Australia and may not apply directly to Cambodian conditions, seasons, or registered products. This edition of the source itself does not list specific pesticide products or rates (noted as intentionally omitted pending updated registrations), so none are reported here either.
